subject: Recap + next actions: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (first discovery)
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Megan Park <megan@synthetix.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next actions: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (first discovery)

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured your priorities correctly and to propose next steps.

Key pain points you described
- Heavy dependency on OpenAI and Anthropic for chat/assistant features (billing and vendor lock).
- Rising token costs and unpredictable latency during peak traffic (affects user experience for live chat).
- Compliance needs: keeping PII out of vendor logs, auditability, and ability to run in a VPC for upcoming contracts.
- Need to preserve function-calling, streaming responses, and tool integrations (search, vectorstore) with minimal changes to product code.

Current stack you shared
- Backend: Scala microservices, serverless lambdas for routing user requests.
- Production models: OpenAI GPT-4o for core assistant flows; Anthropic Claude-instant for sensitive prompts.
- Vector DB: Pinecone for embeddings + search.
- Analytics: internal observability + Sentry for errors.

Success criteria for a migration/POC
- Functional parity for the 3 highest-traffic assistant routes (streaming + function calls).
- <=10% median latency increase vs today under equivalent load (target SLOs to specify in engineering deep-dive).
- Token cost reduction of at least 40% (expected once quantized open models + batching applied).
- Must support VPC deployment and KMS integration for keys.
- Clear rollback path / fallback to existing APIs during rollout.

Initial model shortlist (compatibility-focused)
- Llama 2 70B (4-bit quantized) — good accuracy/latency tradeoff, widely tested.
- Mistral Large / Mixtral variants — strong instruction-following and cheaper at seq lengths you use.
- Falcon-40B/180B trimmed/quantized — candidate for high-throughput ensembles.
- Small Claude/OpenAI-compatible fine-tuned baseline for very latency-sensitive routes (as fallback).

Immediate technical compatibility concerns we noted
- Function calling: we need to map your current function schemas and test Redwood's function-calling shim to avoid code changes.
- Streaming: verify chunking/encoding semantics match your websocket clients.
- KV cache: integration with your session cache and token prefix reuse to minimize recomputation.
- Embeddings parity: sampling a subset of vectors to validate Pinecone search quality.

Deliverables we proposed
1) Technical deep-dive (60–90 min): engineering + infra to map integration points and SLO definitions.
2) Compatibility matrix (we attached a starter CSV) showing supported features per model variant.
3) 3-week POC scope: build adapters for 2 routes, run A/B against your production traffic in canary, cost/latency report.
4) Procurement + legal checklist for Private/VPC deploy options.

Next steps (proposed calendar)
- This week: you to share a short anonymized request trace (10–20 representative sessions) and the function schemas (if OK).
- Wed Aug 27: technical deep-dive with your infra team (Ben + Aditya + your CTO). Can you confirm a 90-min slot?
- Sep 1: Redwood to share final POC scope and cost estimate.

Attachments: compatibility-matrix.csv (starter), redwood-quickstart.pdf (deployment options + SLAs).

If I missed anything or misread priorities, please flag. Otherwise we’ll pencil in Wed Aug 27 at 10am PT as the deep-dive pending your confirmation.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cell: +1 415-555-0198

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference
From: Megan Park <megan@synthetix.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next actions: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (first discovery)

Lauren —

This looks great and accurate. A couple of clarifications:
- We can sanitize the traces (PII removed) and share 20 sessions by tomorrow EOD.
- Our CTO prefers a 60-min deep-dive first (keep it technical but focused on the canary routes). 90 min is fine if you need it.
- Embeddings parity is a gating factor — if search quality drops we will likely reject.

Questions from our side
1) How do you handle model rollbacks if a downstream anomaly appears during canary? Do you provide automatic fallback to the existing OpenAI/Anthropic endpoints?
2) For VPC deployment, what level of telemetry do you require from our side? We are sensitive about sending logs out.

We’re available Wed Aug 27 at 11am PT for the deep-dive. Please send an invite and attendee list.

Thanks,
Megan Park
Head of Product, Synthetix Labs
megan@synthetix.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Megan Park <megan@synthetix.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, cto@synthetix.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next actions: migrating off proprietary LLM APIs (first discovery)

Appreciate the quick reply, Megan. To answer your questions briefly:

Rollback and fallbacks
- Redwood supports policy-based routing: during a canary we can route a percentage of traffic to the Redwood-hosted open-model variant and keep the rest on your current vendor endpoints. If anomalies are detected (latency, error-rate, or QA regressions), we can automatically revert new traffic back to the vendor endpoints while preserving session continuity. We’ll document exact thresholds in the POC SLOs.

Telemetry and VPC
- For Private/VPC deploys we require only minimal telemetry by default (healthchecks, aggregated token counts, sampled error traces). All PII and prompt content can be configured to never leave your VPC; audit logs are customer-controlled and can be pushed to your KMS-protected storage.

I’ll put the Wed Aug 27 11am PT invite on the calendar for a 60-min deep-dive with: Megan, CTO (Synthetix), Lauren, Aditya (inference engineer), and me. Agenda: integration points, function-calling mapping, embeddings parity test plan, and POC acceptance criteria.

Deliverables to share before the call
- Redwood: detailed POC scope + cost estimate (by Sep 1).
- Synthetix: anonymized request traces + function schema (by Aug 26 EOD).

Thanks — excited to dig in.
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
